text.p: Turnover in Australia's financial markets dropped by A$1 trillion in the year to June 30 to around A$27 trillion, the Australian Financial Market Association (AFMA) said in a report released on Thursday.
AFMA said the decline was largely explained by falls in the exchange traded futures and over-the-counter (OTC) markets.
However, within both these sectors some products showed improvement, AFMA said.

There was strong growth in equities turnover value -- up 35 percent -- assisted by stamp duty rationalisation, and steady on-going growth on the bank bill, swaps and currency option markets, the association said.

The declines in bonds and forward rate agreements (FRAs) was largely driven by subdued interest rate volatility, and this was also reflected in a slight reduction turnover in three and 10-year treasury bond futures, AFMA said.
Turnover in long-dated securities was down 25 percent and FRAs down 35 percent, the report said.
The AFMA survey was conducted prior to the cuts in official interest rates in both July and November.
"Overall, Australia's sophisticated financial markets have reached a plateau," AFMA said.
"Infrastructure rationalisation is needed to give than a stronger export oriented impetus ... (and develop) Australia's role as a regional financial centre," the association said.
